Disciplines and Character Paths

A discipline is a field of study. An ability is something you have learned to do with it. Your hero might study Arms to practice martial techniques, Life to restore others, or Scholarship to understand and exploit what others overlook.

Ranks run from 1 to 3 and must be bought in order. There is no level gate on a rank, but the ability you want may require level 3 or 7. Read the requirements before spending: Arms 2 and Subterfuge 1 means you must own both. A rank by itself grants no action, equipment, attribute bonus or unrestricted use of that discipline's cards.

Your class makes some disciplines easier to develop than others. A Blade learns martial techniques readily; an Arcanist has a shorter road into elemental magic. Both can study beyond those strengths. Abilities themselves cost the same DP at each tier, whatever your class.

Buying ranks

You cannot buy disciplines at level 0. After choosing your class, use the table on the following reference page or the prices in your class entry. Each cell lists the separate costs of rank 1 / rank 2 / rank 3, in DP. Buy them in order.

A Blade learning Arms from scratch pays 1 DP for rank 1, then 2 DP for rank 2, then 4 DP for rank 3: 7 DP altogether. That same Blade pays 3, 6 and 12 DP for Life. Odd pays 2 / 4 / 8 DP for every discipline.

The discipline cards below describe each field. These shared purchase rules apply to all eighteen disciplines. Each symbol also appears on ability headers; the small number over its lower edge is the required rank.

Choose a direction

Imagine what you want to do for the company. A healer might protect a retreat, restore HP, treat lasting injuries, or combine all three. A nature-focused hero might become a beast, command an animal, control the ground, or guide companions through dangerous country. These are different choices even when they share a theme.

The four character paths that follow show different ways to build a hero: a Thinking Fighter, Green Healer, Spellblade and Light-Fingered Adventurer. They are examples, not subclasses. Mix them freely where you meet the requirements. The listed cards do not waive DP, tier or discipline requirements, and a suggested future card is not part of your starting equipment.

Keep a few abilities ready for the scenes you expect most often. You may know several attacks, but you still have only the actions you can spend. A useful Maneuver, Reaction, travel skill or social technique can matter more than another similar Main Action.
